# **Pronunciations**

How the terms in this book are said aloud. AuthorLM proposes a row when a filter meets a term it cannot be sure of; you rule on it. A row here is settled: no pass ever rewrites one, and the audio-friendly filter stops flagging its term. Edit freely — here or in the Doc.

| Term | Say it | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Abraxas | uh-BRAK-suss | Gnostic deity name; stress on the middle syllable. |
| Basilides | buh-SIL-ih-deez | Greek proper name; four syllables, stress on the second, final syllable rhymes with 'ease'. |
| Chitta Darshana | CHIT-tuh dar-SHUH-nuh | Sanskrit; the Herdsman's name. Both a's are short; 'sh' as in 'shun', not 'dar-SHAY-na'. |
| Gnostic | NOSS-tik | The initial g is silent — the commonest narrator stumble in this essay. |
| Liber Novus | LEE-bair NOH-vooss | Latin subtitle of The Red Book; long e in 'Liber', not the English 'library' vowel. |
| Pleroma | pleh-ROH-muh | Greek; stress on the second syllable. The initial 'Ple' is short, not 'plee'. |
| Septem Sermones ad Mortuos | SEP-tem ser-MOH-nayss ahd MOR-too-ohss | Latin; the title of Jung's original. Church-Latin reading: 'Sermones' is three syllables, not the English 'sermons'. |
